summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for a flare of chronic pancreatitis with severe abdominal pain and nausea. During the hospitalization, blood cultures identified Klebsiella oxytoca bacteremia, likely originating from her central venous catheter, leading to a diagnosis of sepsis and line-related infection. She was treated with piperacillin-tazobactam and supportive care including IV fluids and pain management with hydromorphone and ketorolac. Imaging studies, including MRI of the jaw and Panorex, showed no osteomyelitis but confirmed extensive dental caries, prompting reactivation of a referral for dental extraction. The patient improved clinically, with resolution of bacteremia on repeat cultures, and was transitioned to oral medications. She was discharged with gabapentin for pain, instructions for central line care with ethanol locks, home health services, and follow-up plans with primary care and oral surgery.
